newsitem.title: IRAN: Zaire asks Iran to help solve dispute with Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Zaire asks Iran to help solve dispute with Rwanda.

text.p: A Zairean minister asked Iran on Wednesday to help solve its dispute with neighbouring Rwanda which has led to a major refugee crisis, the Iranian official news agency IRNA said.
It said Zairean Interior Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda, in a telephone call to Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, "requested Iran to mediate between Zaire and Rwanda."
"Kamanda...called on the Islamic Republic to strive for restoring peace and calm in his country through talks with the U.N. and the Security Council," the agency added.
Velayati said Tehran was ready to help. It was not clear if Zaire had sought direct Iranian mediation, or through the United Nations.
Iran, which has brokered talks on a dispute between Sudan and Uganda, has offered to mediate in the conflict in eastern Zaire which has led to a million refugees being stranded.
Zaire accuses neighbouring Burundi and Rwanda, whose armies are dominated by Tutsis, of backing ethnic Tutsi rebels. Both countries deny the charges.
